A full search of ID61 plus ID91, ID29, ID80, ID39, ID40, ID57, ID63, ID70 and ID73 then found the shape well sourced and the VALUE stated nowhere. OWNER DECLARATION 2026-08-25 (ruling 8) therefore replaces MIGRATED_UNSOURCED: the number is declared on the owner's clinical judgement under OWNER_DECLARED, recorded in owner_declaration, and shown as owner-declared everywhere the dose is served. dose_entries.adjudication: OWNER RULING 2026-08-25: ruled for the repeated-bolus shape. This is austere/prehospital transport, where an infusion pump is often not available, so 0.5 mg/kg IV q20-30min is the executable option and is the preferred answer. JTS ID61's load-then-infuse is NOT rejected — it is recorded as the alternate for pump-capable settings and kept as its own entry, so the guidance is there when the equipment is. owner_declaration.justification: PFC doctrine explicitly prescribes intermittent ketamine push as the no-pump sedation approach for a ventilated patient (JTS ID61 Appendix A Minimum/Better rows, ID80 p.9, ID29 Appendix A) — the SHAPE is sourced. No CPG states a ketamine-alone post-intubation sedation repeat-bolus dose: the cited numbers are either analgesia-labelled (ID61 fn.1 0.1-0.2 mg/kg; ID29 App H 0.1-0.5 mg/kg), a different phase (ID61 App B pre-intubation procedural maintenance), or route-mismatched (ID91 IM/IN). 0.5 mg/kg q20-30min IV is declared on clinical judgement as the practical austere dose, sitting between the analgesia band and the induction band.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25: retired. 2 mg/kg IM is not an analgesic dose — analgesia is SUB-dissociative. It is the dissociative sedation dose mislabelled, and it does not even match the IM sedation dose: NASEMSO gives 4 mg/kg IM (adult) and 3 mg/kg IM (paediatric) for agitation, while 2 mg/kg is the adult IV sedation dose. So it is the IV sedation number on the IM route, labelled analgesia. Unsourced, and superseded by the sub-dissociative entries.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25: retired as unsourced. 0.3 mg/kg came from the hardcode; the sub-dissociative range is covered by NASEMSO's 0.25 mg/kg and JTS ID61's 0.1-0.2 mg/kg, which the owner ruled are the same clinical range.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25: not retired as wrong — recorded as the ALTERNATE on the primary entry instead of standing as a second servable adult dose. JTS ID40 (2021) gives 1 mg/kg; the owner ruled for JTS ID39 (2026), which is newer and corroborates prevailing prehospital practice.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25: retired on safety grounds. The flat 2 mg/kg applied to every paediatric patient is 33% high on a 7-year-old against JTS ID39, which bands it: 2 mg/kg under 5 years, 1.5 mg/kg at 5 and above. Replaced by the two banded entries.
